title: Relative Trivial Cyclic Map
statement: For arbitrary $R$, profinite $H$ and continuous v:$Z$ to $H$, put $G$=1. Define the restricted trivial regular $G$ times $Z$ module, its single-complex cyclic total and its unique forgotten isomorphism to the complex [$R$ to-zero $R$], fixed by the first degree-zero and second degree-one coordinates. Define the identity-underlying forgetting isomorphism from the trivial 1 times $H$ module to the trivial $H$ module, and its derived source comparison using normalized relative-to-scalar invariants. Define trivialCyclicMap as the relative c transported by these source and target identifications. All identities use the actual regular module, its single-complex coordinate maps and canonical exact-functor localization comparisons. Uses [def-sfb-relative-derived-invariants], [def-sfb-relative-cyclic-total], [def-sfb-relative-invariant-forgetting], [def-sfb-relative-bar-data].

proof.text: For the single complex of the restricted trivial regular module, the positive generator endomorphism is the identity in every degree. In degree zero, the identity satisfies the sectionwise characterization in generatorEndExist, so uniqueness gives equality. In other degrees the single complex is zero, and so is its image under retainResidual; all its endomorphisms agree.

Apply TotalModel.differential to this single complex. Its differential is zero and T minus identity is zero by step 1, so the displayed biproduct lift is zero. Cancel the coordinate isomorphisms to prove that the total differential is zero. Outside degrees zero and one, both coordinate summands are zero. Additive retention and forgetting preserve zero objects, so the forgotten total is zero there too.

The extension by zero of trivialCyclic has zero terms outside degrees zero and one: for nonnegative degrees use extendXIso and the explicit object formula; negative degrees are outside the embedding image. Its differential from zero to one is the extension of the specified zero differential; every other adjacent differential has a zero source or target.

In degree zero compose the total coordinate isomorphism, the inverse of isoBiprodZero on the second zero summand, and the single-complex self identification; apply forgetAction and the inverse of extendXIso. In degree one use isoZeroBiprod on the first zero summand instead. In other degrees use the unique isomorphism between the two zero objects. Both differentials are zero by steps 2 and 3, so HomologicalComplex.Hom.isoOfComponents assembles these into a chain isomorphism. The two component formulas are precisely the required normalization equations. Any other normalized isomorphism has the same components in degrees zero and one by cancellation of extendXIso, and has the same components elsewhere since the target term is zero. Componentwise extensionality proves uniqueness.

For forgetTrivialExist, restriction of the trivial regular action is definitionally the trivial regular action, so Iso.refl supplies existence and the underlying identity equation. Two such isomorphisms have the same hom by subtype extensionality from that equation; isomorphism extensionality proves uniqueness. The existing constructions trivialTotalIso, forgetTrivial, trivialSourceIso and trivialCyclicMap then retain their original definitions.
